subject.title: fix(agents): harden exec auto-review shell approval

question: Should OpenClaw make startup-capable login-shell wrappers uniformly fail closed to explicit human approval in auto mode, accepting that existing wrapper-based workflows will no longer receive model auto-approval?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes a security and compatibility boundary across core and plugin-facing execution paths; green tests establish implementation behavior but cannot choose the permanent authorization policy.

options.title: Adopt the fail-closed boundary
options.body: Rebase or refresh the PR, verify the focused shell-wrapper proof on the merge result, and merge the shared human-approval rule.

options.title: Preserve auto-review compatibility
options.body: Keep existing login-shell auto-review behavior and define a different, explicitly approved authorization model before changing these paths.

recommendation.title: Adopt the fail-closed boundary
recommendation.body: Rebase or refresh the PR, verify the focused shell-wrapper proof on the merge result, and merge the shared human-approval rule.

likelyOwner.reason: The current contributor documented the cross-boundary design and upstream Codex-contract review; final policy ownership should be confirmed by the protected maintainer workflow.
